review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Use project money helpers for rounding
item.description: Team convention requires rounding money via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to cent), not Python round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
item.content: Before returning any monetary Decimal, wrap the computation in the repo's round_money helper. Python's round() and bare quantize() use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Read existing module helpers before implementing
item.description: The invoice module already imported ZERO, round_money, and to_money; reusing them satisfies conventions and edge cases.
item.content: Inspect the target file's imports and sibling functions (e.g., line_total, invoice_total) to mirror established patterns like to_money conversion and ZERO as the sum seed.

item.title: Handle empty-collection edge case explicitly
item.description: Guard against division by zero when the invoice has no lines by returning ZERO before dividing.
item.content: Compute total_quantity first; if it is falsy, return ZERO immediately. This matches the spec that an invoice without lines has an average of zero.
